success_patterns: The answer is the entity that recurs across nearly all passages together with the clue's distinctive details (Milne + 'bear of very little brain' -> Winnie-the-Pooh; Richard James + spring falling off a table -> Slinky). The agent took it from that repetition and did not over-think it.

When the clue contained a quoted line (a poem opening) and one passage reproduced it verbatim, the agent used the clue's descriptor ('folklore guy') and the text around the quote (page tags, adjacent words such as 'tags: ... bluebeard') to find the named entity, even though no passage said 'the answer is X'.
The answer was given in the bare headline form the title passages use, keeping hyphens ('Winnie-the-Pooh'), with no role words or descriptors added ('toy', 'character', 'poem').

The answers matched the clue's slot noun ('this toy' -> Slinky, 'this character' -> a character name, 'this folklore guy' -> a folklore figure). Each was a single short proper name, not a related work or an anchor word from the clue.

patch.reasoning: Rule 3 covers verbatim archive hits followed by an answer, but not the case where the clue's quoted line appears verbatim with no answer next to it. In Trajectory 3 the answer came from the clue's descriptor plus nearby tags or text. That case is common for quote, poem and first-line clues, so it is worth stating. A short form note on keeping the hyphenated headline form of a title or character supports the stable pass in Trajectory 1 without adding a blanket shorten or lengthen rule. Neither edit touches the protected block or Rule 3's override, and neither adds a mandatory template. Earlier rejected steps showed that such templates regress stable passes.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - QUOTED-LINE clues ('"This door you might not open, and you did" begins a poem about this folklore guy', 'a poem/song/speech that begins "..."'): the quoted words are only the search key. When a passage repeats them verbatim but no answer is attached, read the text around the quote (neighbouring sentences, page tags, titles, labels such as 'tags: ...') for a named entity that fits the clue's descriptor ('folklore guy' -> a folklore figure). Answer with that entity's standard name (Bluebeard), not the poem, the poet or the quote.

edits.target: - For titles, give the standard title without quotation marks and keep internal punctuation as written in the context ('M*A*S*H', not 'MASH film').
edits.content: - For a famous character or work named in the passage headlines (Wikipedia-style titles such as 'Winnie-the-Pooh - Wikipedia'), copy the headline form with its hyphens and capitals ('Winnie-the-Pooh'), not an alternate form ('Pooh Bear') or a descriptor added to it.
